extracted.intended_audience: CPP administrators, appeals officers, legal advisers, and claimants
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for Canada Pension Plan benefit decisions, reviews, and appeals (initial decisions, reconsideration, appeal to Minister, and appeal to Review Committee), including required documents, time limits, decision-writing and control measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of notice wording
rubrics_metrics.description: The wording of the notice must avoid ambiguity that could create the impression of two distinct courses of recourse (informal reconsideration vs formal appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the last paragraph of decision notices clearly and accurately describes available remedies and the nature of each (e.g., request for reconsideration v. appeal to the Minister). Avoid elliptical language that may confuse lay claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Disability Assessment intelligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Statement of Disability Assessment' appended to refusal letters should explain, intelligibly to the layman, the criteria (section 43(2)) by which the Board ruled on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on paraphrase of statutory text or implicit references to caselaw; provide clear connection between the medical analysis and the legal criteria so the applicant can understand why the condition was not deemed 'severe and prolonged.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision notification must be in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifications of decisions must be in writing (the Act requires written notice, though it may not always require reasons be given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, negative decisions are accompanied by reasons and reminders about appeal rights. For appeals to the Minister, the Act requires reasons; draft letters should follow form-letters where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reasons and appeal information for negative decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Act may not always mandate reasons for initial decisions, negative decisions should include an indication of reasons for refusal and information about appeal rights (e.g., appeal to Minister under section 83).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form-letters accompanying negative decisions should explain how statutory criteria apply to the claimant's facts and outline subsequent procedural steps and timelines for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim benefit fixation when earnings data delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: If final pension amount cannot be computed due to delays in earnings data from the Department of National Revenue, the Director General may fix interim benefits to be adjusted later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document interim calculations and notify beneficiary that amounts are provisional and subject to adjustment upon receipt of definitive earnings data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to assign benefit management to third party
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General may decide to whom benefits of a claimant incapable of managing his own affairs shall be paid (i.e., entrust management to another person or institution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the authority and justification for entrusting management; ensure legal safeguards for incapacitated beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review on new facts (section 86(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions may be reviewed and amended on the ground of new facts presented by either the beneficiary or discovered by the Department; a refused claimant may adduce new facts later without filing a new application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept and consider new facts irrespective of which party introduces them; allow reconsideration even long after initial decision when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of review powers (practical assumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the power to review decisions has not always been formally delegated to the Director General, it is logical that delegation to rule on applications implies delegation to revise decisions under the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement internal delegation practices recognizing Director General authority to review, while noting any formal delegation gaps in documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing beneficiary reporting and periodic control questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiaries are required to inform the district office of changes in status (especially return to work) and receive a control questionnaire at least once a year; questionnaire responses prompting concern lead to submission to a Disability Determination Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain procedures to send, collect, evaluate questionnaires annually and refer cases to the Board when file review suggests reassessment is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability Determination Board powers and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: On review, the Board may require the beneficiary to submit to a medical examination (at CPP cost), provide a medical report or statements about occupation/earnings, or undergo rehabilitation measures; failure to satisfy requirements may forfeit benefits unless the examination poses serious threat to life or health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure beneficiaries are informed of required cooperation, provide CPP-funded exams when ordered, and only accept refusal for legitimate health risk reasons; document noncompliance consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal interview by district office on Board request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board believes a personal interview might develop new information, it may request a district office agent to hold such an interview and report back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate district office interviews timely and include findings in the reassessment file submitted to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassessment reports to Director General
rubrics_metrics.description: After reassessment, the Board should submit a report to the Director General explaining the grounds for altering (or confirming) the initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must explain factual and medical bases for recommended changes and supply clear grounds for any modification to facilitate Director General decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical recordkeeping on determinations and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administration should maintain statistics on applications received, withdrawals, negative decision rates, number of re-examinations, appeals, and medical-diagnosis distributions among beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and analyze statistics annually to monitor workload (e.g., number of initial applications, reassessments, appeals) and to identify trends (e.g., appeal rates, success rates by benefit type).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retirement pension eligibility and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Retirement pension eligibility: contributor aged 65 is entitled; issues may arise re proof of age, period of contribution, start date, and pension amount. Amount is calculated on average monthly income during contribution period and recorded in Record of Earnings; entries can be challenged within four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require applications on prescribed forms with supporting proof of age and earnings; allow challenges to recorded earnings only within statutory four-year window; treat retirement pension calculations as essentially mathematical decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surviving spouse pension designation rules (section 63)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surviving spouse pension eligibility is straightforward except where designation of the surviving spouse (legal v common-law) is disputed; the Minister retains discretionary power to substitute a common-law spouse under section 63, with simplified conditions in revised form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply section 63 carefully, consider cohabitation and representation evidence when relevant, and maintain continuing control for events (e.g., remarriage) that interrupt payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orphan's benefits objective conditions and attendance checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for orphan's benefits is objective but depends on continued checks on the orphan's attendance at school as part of ongoing eligibility verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement periodic verification of school attendance and other dependency criteria to maintain entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death benefits lump-sum payment issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Death benefits are generally paid as lump sums into contributor estates; primary disputes involve length of contributing period and amount payable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require clear proof of contributing period and supporting documentation to compute death benefit amounts accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications must be on prescribed legal forms with supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for benefits must be made in accordance with prescribed legal forms; mere request for information is insufficient. Applications must be in writing, accompanied by supporting documents (proof of age, statements of earnings/contributions, proof of death), and cannot be presented by telephone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train district offices to ensure all required documents are collected and transmitted centrally; reject informal or incomplete submissions that do not comply with prescribed forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactivity limits for benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no universal time limit for submission of applications, but surviving-spouse and orphan applications cannot be retroactive beyond 12 months; retirement pensions had no retroactivity prior to Jan 1, 1978 but thereafter may be retroactive up to 11 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform applicants of applicable retroactivity restrictions and compute effective dates accordingly; watch legislative change dates for different rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial file processing and escalation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims and Benefits Division opens a file under the claimant's number; rapid examination usually suffices. Difficult cases prompt a first-examiner report and referral to an audit and review section; thorny issues are referred to a reconsideration committee (head of Claims and Benefits, head of Legal Services, advisor to Director General). The committee cannot rule unless unanimous; if not unanimous the Director General decides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document referrals and reports; seek unanimity for committee rulings and prepare for Director General decision when unanimity absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of alternative proof of age and ad hoc tribunals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General may accept proof of age used for Old Age Security or Family Allowances, consult Statistics Canada, or as final resort, constitute an ad hoc tribunal whose decision is conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ordered sequence for uncertain proofs of age and record the basis for accepting alternative evidence; use ad hoc tribunal only as last resort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Minister: filing location and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal to the Minister (section 83) must be initiated by written request addressed to central administration (Deputy Minister of Social Welfare) and must be lodged within one year following the decision. Communications within the year that show intent are treated as appeals; after one year they may be interpreted as review requests if new facts are invoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralize receipt of appeals; screen incoming correspondence for intent and timeliness; advise appellants of correct filing address and one-year deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized persons may file appeals on behalf of claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister can authorize a person other than the applicant to file an appeal on the applicant's behalf if the applicant is incapable of managing his affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records of any authorization and ensure appeals filed by authorized persons meet procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary verification by Appeals Section and summary rejection if facts missing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Appeals Section must verify fundamental factual elements in the file (e.g., proof of age, sufficient contributions). If essential proofs are missing, the appeal may be summarily rejected without studying substantive eligibility arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a preliminary completeness check before substantive consideration; notify appellants to supply missing essential documentation to avoid summary rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent reassessment by a new Disability Determination Board on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: For disability appeals the file is placed before a Disability Determination Board whose physician-members did not participate in the initial evaluation; the Board considers new circumstances, may order new medical exams or specialist consultations, and reports with recommendation to Appeals Section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Board is composed of independent physician-members, update medical evidence as needed, and include Board recommendations in draft decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-letter draft decisions explaining statutory criteria and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft decisions generally conform to specific form-letters that for negative decisions explain re-examination of documents, the meaning of 'severe and prolonged disability', analyze submitted facts, invite new applications if situations change, inform of right to challenge within 90 days before a Review Committee, and outline where notice of appeal must be sent and what information it should contain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardized form-letters but ensure they tailor the explanation of statutory criteria to the appellant's facts and explicitly set out procedural steps and timelines for further recourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness expectation for Minister reconsideration ('forthwith')
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 83(2) requires the Minister to reconsider the initial decision 'forthwith', though in practice introduction of new facts and control measures often slow the procedure; empirical averages show delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to proceed promptly and document reasons for delay; track time between initial decision and appeal decision to monitor compliance with 'forthwith' expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Review Committee is contentious review with procedural regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal under section 84 to the Review Committee is a contentious review before an authority outside the Department; unlike previous phases it is governed by fairly elaborate regulations under section 91(1)(c) and internal rules impart a more formal character to the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow statutory/regulatory procedural provisions closely when compiling files and preparing hearings for Review Committees to ensure fairness and perceived independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal to Review Committee: timing, content, and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of appeal must be in writing to the Director General within 90 days of transmission of the Minister's decision (Director General may extend). The notice must identify the appellant (and contributor where relevant), state the date of notification of the first appeal, present reasons and pertinent facts, identify the person who has accepted appointment to act on the Review Committee, and may be joint when two parties have similar reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appellants with clear instructions and checklists for notices of appeal; record and verify dates to determine timeliness and whether an extension is needed or granted; require adequate statement of facts to acquaint the Committee with appellant's point of view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director General's discretion to extend time limits and non-reviewability of refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General may extend the 90-day time limit; refusal to extend is discretionary and cannot be challenged before a Review Committee unless an abuse of discretion is alleged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent exercise of discretion with documented reasons; be mindful that refusal may only be judicially attackable on abuse of discretion grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant influence on Review Committee composition and perception of independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Director General forms the Review Committee, steps should be taken so the appellant exerts influence on the composition to avoid the impression the Committee is a 'creature of the Department.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appellants with information about committee membership options and selection mechanisms to preserve perceived independence and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of case file for Review Committee hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Appeals Section coordinates compilation of the file for the Review Committee; the course and sequence of operations differ depending on whether the case involves disability pensions or disputes between legal and common-law spouses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble a complete, chronological file including prior decisions, medical reports, Board reports, and appellant submissions; adapt preparation steps to the case category to ensure the Committee has full context.
